summary: Configured node1’s local PAM authentication to lock accounts after five failed attempts and automatically unlock after 300 seconds. Verified behavior before and after a successful node reboot.
actions_performed: Set deny = 5 and unlock_time = 300 in /etc/security/faillock.conf; preserved a rollback copy.
Verified four failures still permit authentication, while five failures lock the account.
Verified automatic authentication recovery 307 seconds after lock confirmation.
Rebooted node1 once and confirmed a changed boot identity, healthy system state, persistent configuration, and working lockout behavior.
Removed all disposable accounts, generated credentials, and temporary validation files.

evidence.requirement: Five failed attempts trigger account lockout
evidence.summary: The active policy contains deny=5; direct PAM testing succeeded after four failures and denied the correct password after five.

evidence.requirement: Account automatically unlocks after five minutes
evidence.summary: The active policy contains unlock_time=300; timed testing showed immediate denial while locked and successful authentication 307 seconds after lock confirmation.

Baseline boot ID fe6e58b2-7e4d-4e8a-b1d7-3a15564059bb was healthy; reboot was acknowledged, connectivity reset, and node1 returned with boot ID 9e2b9354-165e-47e1-bcc3-57c9a86bf8ce. Post-restart health and live lockout tests passed.
node1 is running with zero failed units, exactly one deny=5 and unlock_time=300 directive, three active pam_faillock hooks, and no validation artifacts.
